title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to measure the incremental detection benefit of adding automated sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-produced intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the declared/requested model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory items drawn from a deterministic task generator spanning three vendor-CLI families and three topology templates. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 (0.9986111); the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation, with a single allowed repair-stage call) flagged 720/720 (1.0). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0013889; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10k resamples, seed 1729) = [0.0, 0.0041667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair). The observed effect lies far below our preregistered minimum effect of interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact artifact-grounded outcomes, a Methods clarification reconciling provider-call audit fields, and an evidence-grounded interpretation that the negligible guarded benefit arises from a validator ceiling effect in this curated regime. We point readers to the archived execution manifest and per-episode artifacts for independent verification.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Practical operational assurance demands that generated artifacts satisfy syntactic correctness, command-ordering/workflow constraints, and higher-order safety policies. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators might miss. Prior surveys and system reports advocate such workflow-centred mitigations [1]–[3], but provide limited preregistered, paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution. To quantify that marginal contribution in a controlled way, we preregistered and ran a paired study that enforces shared_initial_candidate semantics: the identical sampled generation is evaluated by (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation and a single permitted repair invocation. Our core research question is: under these controlled semantics and a curated task bank, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline)? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete accounting; (3) a concise Methods clarification reconciling provider-call audit fields; (4) an evidence-grounded interpretation explaining the near-zero marginal effect and operational boundary conditions.
sections.related_work: Work combining LLM generation with external validators, emulators, and repair loops has grown rapidly. Recent surveys and architectural overviews argue that correctness in intent→configuration pipelines is multidimensional and that layered V&V (static analysis plus emulation or sandboxing) is a practical mitigation pattern [1]. Tool-focused case studies trace the expanding capabilities and limits of static verifiers for configuration analysis and show why emulator-assisted validation is often recommended to catch dynamic, stateful, or timing-dependent behaviors that static rule sets miss [2]. Prototype systems integrating generation with verification report heterogeneous gains: sometimes a verifier alone catches most dangerous errors, while in other regimes emulation uncovers subtle runtime failures [3]. Those findings motivated our paired design: by reusing the identical sampled candidate across conditions we isolate only downstream effects (emulation observations or permitted repair) rather than conflating them with generation variability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Planned Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440) and a minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20 used for power planning. Inclusion rules required vendor-specific parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; irrecoverable parser failures would be deterministically replaced per the preregistered missingness policy. All analysis choices and multiplicity handling were fixed in the preregistration.

Task bank and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. Confirmatory items were produced deterministically from an intent_configuration_repair_v1 generator spanning three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit intent, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (make-before-break, must-be-down-for-fields, minimum_active_in_groups). For each task we obtained exactly one sampled initial candidate (one provider call) and that identical candidate was evaluated by both conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics), isolating downstream guarded-stage effects.

Validator, emulation, repair and provider-call budget. The baseline validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applies vendor-CLI parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order/workflow constraint checks, protected-interface invariants, group-level activity rules, and final-state conformance. The guarded pipeline runs that validator and then executes the candidate in a sandboxed emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices; the harness translates runtime observations (interface transitions, concurrent-interface states, MTU/VLAN application, observable reachability) into detection triggers not encoded as static rules. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model invocation per task and the confirmatory run recorded exactly one repair-stage call. Model configuration recorded the declared/requested model as "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) with requested max_output_tokens = 2000; the client supplied no explicit temperature parameter (recorded as null). Shared_initial_candidate semantics and the repair limit are crucial for interpreting paired discordances: because generation was shared, any guarded-only detection must arise from either (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation not encoded as a validator violation or (ii) a permitted repair invocation that changed scoring.

Provider-call audit fields: clarification and reconciliation. The execution manifest and deterministic-reconciliation artifacts report the provider-call audit summary used in run accounting. Key verified numbers (from the archived execution/accounting artifacts) are: model_calls_used = 721; hosted_model_call_event_count = 721; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 721; cache_miss_count = 721. The stage_counts breakdown is: shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. The condition_counts fields in the audit (keys labeled "shared" and "guarded") reflect the mapping from provider-call events to logical pipeline stages, not direct episode tallies: the audit labels "shared": 720 correspond to the 720 shared_initial_generation calls (one per paired task) and "guarded": 1 corresponds to the single repair-stage invocation associated with a guarded downstream action. Thus asymmetry in condition_counts arises because most provider calls are the single shared-generation events that are reused by both conditions, whereas the single repair-stage call is attributable only to the guarded pipeline. Deterministic reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 720 and reconciles these audit fields with episode accounting (completed_episode_count = 1440, failed_episode_count = 0). This paragraph provides the explicit artifact-grounded mapping reviewers requested: stage_counts counts provider-call types (shared generation vs. repair) while complete_pair_count counts paired episodes; both views are consistent in the archived manifest.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and inferential outcomes (artifact-grounded). The paired contingency totals (artifact: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) are: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric outputs are reproduced verbatim from the archived analysis results (analysis/results.json).

Discordant-pair attribution. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation record model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics, the unique n10 discordant pair is therefore attributable to the single recorded repair-stage invocation or to a guarded-emulation observation that the validator did not encode. The archived per-episode raw_results.jsonl contains the validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields for that pair and thus permits an auditor to inspect whether the repair changed the candidate or whether the emulation alone produced the guarded detection. The archived reconciliation artifacts confirm that there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per-episode scoring traces (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) show normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count = 0 for the vast majority of shared_initial candidates. Those traces illustrate the validator-ceiling regime: most sampled candidates already satisfied the validator’s rule set and sandboxed emulation corroborated validator findings in the curated task bank.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The artifact-grounded evidence supports three tightly scoped factors. First, validator ceiling effect and task-rule alignment: the deterministic validator explicitly encodes the workflow and policy constraints exercised by the curated tasks (patterns like shutdown_configure_restore and make_before_break_uplink_switchover). The baseline marginal success rate of 719/720 leaves essentially no headroom for additional guarded-stage detections. Second, curated inclusion and reduced adversarial exposure: the confirmatory set required parser acceptance before inclusion and was generated deterministically, so runtime-only failures that emulation reveals in more diverse or adversarial collections are underrepresented. Third, shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity: because generations were reused and only one repair-stage call occurred, observed discordance reduces to a single downstream event, making the aggregate marginal gain necessarily small.

Operational implications. In environments that enforce strong prevalidation and maintain a validator with rules aligned to expected intents, adding blanket sandboxed emulation may yield negligible incremental detection at scale; selective guarding for high-risk changes or adversarially focused testing may be a more efficient allocation of emulation resources. Importantly, our finding is narrowly scoped: it pertains to the declared model, the single validator implementation, the curated task bank, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. Generalization to noisy, adversarial, or broader vendor/CLI regimes requires targeted follow-ups using adversarial task banks and higher-fidelity emulators.

Reproducible audit path. The archived execution manifest and analysis artifacts provide an auditable mapping from reported counts to specific per-episode traces and to the single repair-stage call. Independent auditors can locate the unique discordant pair in the archived raw_results.jsonl and inspect validator_trace and repair_provider_trace objects to determine whether the guarded detection followed an emulation observation or an applied repair. These artifacts are the canonical reproducibility bundle for the run (see Disclosure).
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator against the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a vanishing aggregate detection gain (0.0013889) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0041667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; under shared_initial_candidate semantics this mapping is auditable in the archived per-episode artifacts. We interpret the near-zero aggregate effect as the consequence of validator ceiling effects and the curated inclusion policy. Future work should target adversarial, production-like, and expanded vendor-CLI distributions to identify regimes where guarded emulation yields substantive operational benefit.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministically generated task bank and parser-based inclusion produce limited ecological diversity and a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across alternative models and validator families.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream guarded-stage contributions but remove between-condition generation variability; alternative designs permitting independent guarded re‑generation could yield different paired outcomes.
Emulation fidelity is bounded by the sandbox harness used; higher-fidelity device/control-plane modeling or long-lived stateful interactions could reveal additional runtime-only failures.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a broad negative claim about all NetOps workflows.

Residual provider-side nondeterminism or hidden caching cannot be ruled out entirely despite deterministic reconciliation; these uncertainties are documented in the archived execution and reconciliation artifacts.
